sections.content:
Population change in Exeter in 2032

The population in Exeter is projected to increase from 134,811 people in 2022 to 146,558 people in 2032.

The biggest factor in this population change is net international migration, which will increase the population by 21,357 people.

This is different to the majority of areas in England, where net internal migration is projected to be the biggest factor in population change.

sections.title: Contributors to population change in Exeter
sections.subtitle: How the population is projected to change, by cause
sections.source: Subnational population projections for England from Office for National Statistics – Migration category variant
sections.note: The components of change do not always sum exactly to the total population change in an area. This is primarily due to the effect of constraining the final projections to the National Population Projections for England.

sections.content:
Population change is projected by looking at births and deaths (natural change) and people moving in and out of areas. In Exeter, our projections show that between 2022 and 2032:

  • Births and deaths is not projected to change the population substantially, with 11,826 births and 11,710 deaths in Exeter between 2022 and 2032. There will be an increase of 0.2% in England.
  • Net internal migration (people moving to and from other local authorities in England) is projected to reduce the population by 10,556, with 163,920 people moving to the area and 174,476 people moving from the area between 2022 and 2032. This would decrease the population in Exeter by 7.8%.
  • Net cross-border migration (between UK nations) is projected to increase the population by 1,221, with 8,777 people moving to the area and 7,555 people moving from the area between 2022 and 2032. This would increase the population in Exeter by 0.9%.
  • Net international migration is projected to increase the population by 21,357, with 37,397 people moving to the area and 16,040 people moving from the area between 2022 and 2032. This would increase the population in Exeter by 15.8%, compared with an increase of 6.5% in England.

sections.content:
Age profile in Exeter in 2032

The median age in Exeter is projected to rise from 35 years in 2022 to 36 years in 2032.

In England, the median age is projected to be 41 years in 2032.

In 2032, 17% of the population in Exeter are projected to be aged 65 years or over, up from 16% in 2022.

sections.title: The 40 to 49 age group are set to see the largest change in Exeter between 2022 and 2032
sections.subtitle: Percentages of population by 10 year age bands, 2022 and 2032
sections.source: Subnational population projections for England from Office for National Statistics – Migration category variant

sections.content:
Between 2022 and 2032, the share of the working age population (people aged 16 years to State Pension age) in Exeter is projected to stay the same, at around 70%.

The old age dependency ratio (the number of people of State Pension age for every 1,000 people of working age) is projected to rise from 222 to 232 over the same time period.

This is below average for England in 2032 (287 per 1,000). Nationally, a high old age dependency ratio means more older people are financially reliant on the working age population to pay for pensions.

How will the number of young people change in Exeter?

In 2032, 16% of people are projected to be aged 18 years and under, down from 18% in 2022.

This is below average for England in 2032 (20%).

Looking at the youngest age groups in Exeter between 2022 and 2032, we can see the share of:

  • Infants (aged 0 to 4 years) will stay around the same, at 4%
  • Primary school age children (aged 5 to 11 years) will fall from 7% to 6%
  • Secondary school age children and sixth-form age (aged 12 to 18 years) will stay around the same, at 6%
